question.problem:
For which of the following polynomials is $(x+3)$ a factor?

I. $f(x)=2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-8x+3$

II. $g(x)={x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-x-3$

III. $h(x)={x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-x-2$
question.worked_solution:
The factor theorem states that $(x-r)$ is a factor of a polynomial $p(x)$ if and only if the root $x=r$ is also a root of $p(x).$ 

Here, we are considering $(x+3).$ The root of this expression can be found by setting the expression equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3 & =0 \\ x & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, $(x+3)$ is a factor of $p(x)$ if the root $x=-3$ is a root of $p(x).$ 

So now, we will check if $x=-3$ is a root of the polynomials $f,$ $g$ and $h.$

- Evaluating $x=-3$ at $f(x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) & =2(-3)^{3}+3(-3)^{2}-8(-3)+3 \\  & =2(-27)+3(9)+24+3 \\  & =-54+27+24+3 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, by the factor theorem, we conclude that $(x+3)$ is indeed a factor of $f(x).$

- Now, evaluating $x=-3$ at $g(x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}g(-3) & =(-3)^{3}+3(-3)^{2}-(-3)-3 \\  & =-27+3(9)+3-3 \\  & =-27+27+3-3 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, by the factor theorem, we conclude that $(x+3)$ is indeed a factor of $g(x).$

- Finally, evaluating $x=-3$ at $h(x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}h(-3) & =(-3)^{3}+2(-3)^{2}-(-3)-2 \\  & =-27+2(9)+3-2 \\  & =-27+18+3-2 \\  & =-8\ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
